in.other_title: Stronger trained debaters yield +4 points judge accuracy; no effect for consultants
in.rationale: Khan et al. report that best-of-N and critique-and-refinement make consultants relatively more persuasive for the incorrect answer, lowering judge accuracy. Arnesen et al. find no apparent relationship between trained consultant skill and judge accuracy; Arnesen et al. train Llama3-8B with DPO and use a GPT-4-Turbo judge fine-tuned to be less sycophantic, while Khan et al. use inference-time optimisation with an untrained judge.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: how optimising consultants for persuasiveness affects judge accuracy on QuALITY

in.other_title: Arnesen et al. argue Khan et al.'s consultancy results rest on an overly sycophantic GPT-4T judge
in.rationale: The authors point to a limitation of Khan et al.'s evaluation (a sycophantic judge favouring consultants, and an ambiguous trend at GPT-4 level) rather than reporting a conflicting rerun, so CRITIQUES fits. Their response in this paper is to fine-tune a calibrated judge (Section 3.1).
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether consultancy baselines judged by a prompted GPT-4T are a fair comparison for debate; concerns Khan et al.'s consultancy optimization results

text: The paper reports that under best-of-N and critique-and-refinement optimisation, consultants become relatively more persuasive when arguing the incorrect answer; the authors suggest RLHF-tuned models already argue correct answers well, so optimisation disproportionately improves advocacy for incorrect answers by enabling exploration of deceptive approaches. This degrades judge accuracy because the judge does not know a priori whether the consultant is assigned the correct answer.
title: More persuasive consultants lower judge accuracy; optimisation favours incorrect side
